1. Introduction¶

The visit_summary dataset provides a summary of visit metadata. The visit_summary dataset is available only via the Butler.

  • Butler dataset type: visit_summary
  • number of datasets: 28,698
  • columns: 55

This notebook demonstrates how to access the visit_summary dataset, and compares its structure and contents to those available in the VisitDetector tables.

Related tutorials: 104.4. Catalog queries with the Butler demonstrates how to access tabular information using the Butler. 204.3 Astrometric Calibration and 205.2 PSF for visits demonstrate how to retrieve the WCS and the PSF model using the visit_summary dataset. 208.1. LSSTCam focal plane provides information on the geometry of the LSSTCam detectors.

1.1. Import packages¶

Import standard python packages numpy and matplotlib. From the lsst package, import modules for accessing the Butler from the LSST Science Pipelines (pipelines.lsst.io) and setting the plotstyle. Also import lsst packages to work with WCS and PSF models, and to access properties of LSSTCam.

In [1]:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.collections import PatchCollection
from matplotlib.patches import Polygon

from lsst.daf.butler import Butler
from lsst.utils.plotting import set_rubin_plotstyle
from lsst.images import SkyProjection, DetectorFrame, Box
from lsst.images.psfs import PointSpreadFunction
from lsst.obs.lsst import LsstCam

1.2. Define parameters and functions¶

Instantiate a Butler for DP2 and check it.

In [2]:
butler = Butler("dp2", collections="dp2")
assert butler is not None

Set up the default rubin plotstyle.

In [3]:
set_rubin_plotstyle()

2. Columns¶

2.1. Descriptions and units¶

The visit_summary dataset type contains one dataset per visit. Each visit dataset is an ExposureCatalog tabular object from the LSST Science Pipelines lsst.afw.table module which provides handlers for data, catalogs, and data records. An ExposureCatalog consists of one ExposureRecord per detector processed for the visit (i.e. an ExposureRecord is a table row). These objects contain tabular data and methods specific to the processing of exposures in the pipelines. The tabular data consists of 55 columns containing information on the visit-detector metadata and statistics. The table below provides the data type, description and units for each column.

name dtype description unit
id int64 unique ID
bbox_min_x int32 bounding box (minimum) pix
bbox_min_y int32 bounding box (minimum) pix
bbox_max_x int32 bounding box (maximum) pix
bbox_max_y int32 bounding box (maximum) pix
visit int64 Visit number
physical_filter <U32 Physical filter
band <U32 Name of band
psfSigma float32 PSF model second-moments determinant radius (center of chip) (pixel) pix
psfArea float32 PSF model effective area (center of chip) (pixel**2) pix2
psfIxx float32 PSF model Ixx (center of chip) (pixel**2) pix2
psfIyy float32 PSF model Iyy (center of chip) (pixel**2) pix2
psfIxy float32 PSF model Ixy (center of chip) (pixel**2) pix2
raCorners float64 Right Ascension of bounding box corners (degrees) deg
decCorners float64 Declination of bounding box corners (degrees) deg
ra float64 Right Ascension of bounding box center (degrees) deg
dec float64 Declination of bounding box center (degrees) deg
zenithDistance float32 Zenith distance of bounding box center (degrees) deg
pixelScale float32 Measured detector pixel scale (arcsec/pixel) arcsec / pix
expTime float32 Exposure time of the exposure (seconds) s
zeroPoint float32 Mean zeropoint in detector (mag) mag
skyBg float32 Average sky background (ADU) adu
skyNoise float32 Average sky noise (ADU) adu
meanVar float32 Mean variance of the weight plane (ADU**2) adu2
astromOffsetMean float32 Mean offset of astrometric calibration matches (arcsec) arcsec
astromOffsetStd float32 Standard deviation of offsets of astrometric calibration matches (arcsec) arcsec
nPsfStar int32 Number of stars used for PSF model
psfStarDeltaE1Median float32 Median E1 residual (starE1 - psfE1) for psf stars
psfStarDeltaE2Median float32 Median E2 residual (starE2 - psfE2) for psf stars
psfStarDeltaE1Scatter float32 Scatter (via MAD) of E1 residual (starE1 - psfE1) for psf stars
psfStarDeltaE2Scatter float32 Scatter (via MAD) of E2 residual (starE2 - psfE2) for psf stars
psfStarDeltaSizeMedian float32 Median size residual (starSize - psfSize) for psf stars (pixel) pix
psfStarDeltaSizeScatter float32 Scatter (via MAD) of size residual (starSize - psfSize) for psf stars (pixel) pix
psfStarScaledDeltaSizeScatter float32 Scatter (via MAD) of size residual scaled by median size squared
psfTraceRadiusDelta float32 Delta (max - min) of the model psf trace radius values evaluated on a grid of unmasked pixels (pixel). pix
psfApFluxDelta float32 Delta (max - min) of the model psf aperture flux (with aperture radius of max(2, 3*psfSigma)) values evaluated on a grid of unmasked pixels.
psfApCorrSigmaScaledDelta float32 Delta (max - min) of the model psf aperture correction factors scaled (divided) by the psfSigma evaluated on a grid of unmasked pixels.
maxDistToNearestPsf float32 Maximum distance of an unmasked pixel to its nearest model psf star (pixel). pix
starEMedian float32 Median ellipticity (sqrt(starE1**2.0 + starE2**2.0)) of the stars used in the PSF model.
starUnNormalizedEMedian float32 Median un-normalized ellipticity (sqrt((starXX - starYY)**2.0 + (2.0*starXY)**2.0)) of the stars used in the PSF model.
effTime float32 Effective exposure time calculated from psfSigma, skyBg, and zeroPoint (seconds). s
effTimePsfSigmaScale float32 PSF scaling of the effective exposure time.
effTimeSkyBgScale float32 Sky background scaling of the effective exposure time.
effTimeZeroPointScale float32 Zeropoint scaling of the effective exposure time.
magLim float32 Magnitude limit at SNR=5 (M5) calculated from psfSigma, skyBg, zeroPoint, and readNoise. mag
preliminary_wcs_detector_pointing_residual float64 Maximum difference (on the pointing-fit grid) between the target WCS position and the position predicted by camera geometry, after re-pointing using the target WCS for this detector only. rad
preliminary_wcs_visit_pointing_residual float64 Maximum difference (on the pointing-fit grid) between the target WCS position and the position predicted by camera geometry, after re-pointing using the target WCS of all non-rejected detectors in the visit. rad
preliminary_wcs_detector_pointing_rejected bool Flag set if this detector was rejected from the pointing fit due to its wcs_detector_pointing_residual value.
wcsSkypixId int64 ID of the skypix pixel that provided the WCS.
wcs_corner_max_offset float64 Maximum on-sky difference between the input-summary WCS and the wcs_provider WCS at detector corners. rad
wcs_detector_pointing_residual float64 Maximum difference (on the pointing-fit grid) between the target WCS position and the position predicted by camera geometry, after re-pointing using the target WCS for this detector only. rad
wcs_visit_pointing_residual float64 Maximum difference (on the pointing-fit grid) between the target WCS position and the position predicted by camera geometry, after re-pointing using the target WCS of all non-rejected detectors in the visit. rad
wcs_detector_pointing_rejected bool Flag set if this detector was rejected from the pointing fit due to its wcs_detector_pointing_residual value.
wcs_sip_delta_sky float64 Maximum pixel-to-sky difference between the WCS and its FITS TAN-SIP approximation. rad
wcs_sip_delta_pixel float64 Maximum sky-to-pixel difference between the WCS and its FITS TAN-SIP approximation. pix

The visit_summary schema is currently not available at https://sdm-schemas.lsst.io/, although many of its columns are also present in the VisitDetector table. The schema information in the table above is extracted directly from the ExposureCatalog object via astropy (see section 4.4.).

2.2. Key columns¶

Descriptions for a few of the columns that are the most commonly used.

2.2.1 Identifiers¶

Integers that uniquely identify the detector (CCD) and visit.

  • id
  • visit

2.2.2. Coordinates¶

The sky coordinates in decimal degrees of the center of the detector.

  • ra
  • dec

The RA, Dec of the four corners of the corresponding detector are available as arrays corresponding to lower left, upper left, upper right, lower right corners in that order.

  • raCorners
  • decCorners

2.2.3. Observation metadata¶

The name of the filter (bandpass) that was used for the observation. There is also the column physical_filter which is unique to the physical filter (i.e., the coated glass plate). There is only one glass filter per band ($ugrizy$).

  • band

The airmass, $X$, can be calculated from the zenith angle, $z$, as $X=sec(z)$.

  • zenithDistance

2.2.4. Image characterization¶

Some of the derived properties of the corresponding visit_image for the detector.

  • skyBG
  • magLim
  • psfSigma
  • effTime

3. Comparison to VisitDetector¶

As mentioned previously visit_summary is a Butler only dataset that is similar to the VisitDetector table which can be queried via TAP and Butler. This means there are differences in how these datasets are structured and best utilised. Furthermore there are also slight differences in the columns stored in these datasets.

3.1. Dataset structure¶

It is noted in tutorial 104.4 Catalog queries with the Butler that the Butler provides access to the tables as they are stored in parquet format and so querying and subsetting capabilities can be limited compared to TAP. Therefore the structure of visit_summary means that it is best suited for getting information on all detectors on a per visit basis. By comparison VisitDetector is more suited for queries that span multiple visits.

3.2. Column names¶

3.2.1. Columns with different names¶

The majority of columns have the same names between visit_summary and VisitDetector. The following columns are the same but with slightly different names, in particular the column names used to identify the visit and detector:

visit_summary column name VisitDetector column name
id detector
visit visitId
raCorners llcra, ulcra, urcra, lrcra
decCorners llcdec, ulcdec, urcdec, lrcdec
wcs_corner_max_offset wcsCornerMaxOffset
wcs_detector_pointing_residual wcsDetectorPointingResidual
wcs_visit_pointing_residual wcsVisitPointingResidual
preliminary_wcs_detector_pointing_residual wcsPreliminaryDetectorPointingResidual
preliminary_wcs_visit_pointing_residual wcsPreliminaryVisitPointingResidual

Warning: In visit_summary the Ra, Dec positions of detector corners are stored as arrays in the raCorners and decCorners columns. In VisitDetector each corner has it own column (ll: lower left, ul: upper left, ur: upper right, lr: lower right) for Ra and Dec.

Warning: The wcs type columns have units of radians in visit_summary and units of arcsec in VisitDetector.

3.2.2. Columns unique to visit_summary¶

The following columns are available in visit_summary and not VisitDetector:

  • bbox_min_x
  • bbox_min_y
  • bbox_max_x
  • bbox_max_y
  • psfArea
  • psfIxx
  • psfIyy
  • psfIxy
  • meanVar
  • preliminary_wcs_detector_pointing_rejected
  • wcsSkypixId
  • wcs_detector_pointing_rejected
  • wcs_sip_delta_sky
  • wcs_sip_delta_pixel

3.2.3. Columns unique to VisitDetector¶

The following columns are available in VisitDetector and not visit_summary:

  • seeing
  • skyRotation
  • expMidpt
  • expMidptMJD
  • obsStart
  • obsStartMJD
  • darkTime
  • xSize
  • ySize

3.3. Additional information in visit_summary¶

The ExposureCatalog object can be used to derive schema information for each column in addition to the tabular data. Furthermore the constituent ExposureRecord objects contain methods for extracting the World Coordinate System (WCS) and Point Spread Function (PSF) models for a given visit-detector. Examples of extracting this information are provided in section 4.

Warning: As detailed in tutorials 204.3. and 205.2. it is expected that the WCS and PSF information will be more commonly accessed from a detector's visit_image data directly. This image data is not currently available in "Early DP2" but will be available with the "Full DP2" release.

4. Data access¶

The visit_summary table is only available via Butler. The dimensions for the visit_summary table are band, instrument, day_obs, physical_filter, visit, with instrument and visit being required dimensions.

In [4]:
butler.get_dataset_type("visit_summary")
Out[4]:
DatasetType('visit_summary', {band, instrument, day_obs, physical_filter, visit}, ExposureCatalog)
In [5]:
butler.get_dataset_type("visit_summary").dimensions.required
Out[5]:
{instrument, visit}

4.1. Read in the dataset¶

The visit_summary dataset is a catalog with a dataset entry for each visit.

Warning: To inspect the full list of 28,698 datasets for DP2 uncomment the line below to override the default limit = 20000 when calling butler.query_datasets.

In [6]:
dataset_refs = butler.query_datasets(
    "visit_summary",
    # limit = None
)
len(dataset_refs)

lsst.daf.butler._butler WARNING: More datasets are available than the requested limit of 20000.
Out[6]:
20000

Inspect the identifying information for the first visit returned by the query.

In [7]:
dataset_refs[0].dataId
Out[7]:
{instrument: 'LSSTCam', visit: 2025042400172, band: 'r', day_obs: 20250424, physical_filter: 'r_57'}

Retrieve the ExposureCatalog dataset for the visit.

In [8]:
ref = dataset_refs[0]
visit_summary = butler.get(ref)
In [9]:
visit_summary

Clean up.

In [10]:
del dataset_refs, ref, visit_summary

4.2. Example query by spatial constraint¶

The Butler can be queried with various constraints (see also tutorial 104.4.). As an example, search for visits that overlap a position of RA = 150.1 degrees and Dec = 2.1 degrees.

In [11]:
ra_targ = 150.1
dec_targ = 2.1

Define the where statement and bind parameters.

In [12]:
query = "visit.region OVERLAPS POINT(:ra, :dec)"
bind_params = {"ra": ra_targ, "dec": dec_targ}

Run the Butler query with spatial constraints.

In [13]:
dataset_refs = butler.query_datasets(
    "visit_summary", where=query, bind=bind_params
)
len(dataset_refs)
Out[13]:
716

Retrieve the visit_summary for the first visit in the query.

Warning: When using butler.get it is usually advised to limit the returned columns via the parameters dictionary. This does not currently work with ExposureCatalog; uncomment the line below to see the KeyError being raised.

In [14]:
ref = dataset_refs[0]
visit_summary = butler.get(
    ref,
    # parameters={"columns":
    #             ["id", "visit", "raCorners", "decCorners", "magLim"]
    #             }
)
In [15]:

4.3. Read ExposureCatalog as a table¶

The ExposureCatalog can be converted to an astropy table using the asAstropy() method. This table contains a row for each detector processed in the visit.

Warning: Some detectors may be missing or have NaN entries depending on whether or not they could be fully processed by the pipeline.

In [17]:
visit_summary_tab = visit_summary.asAstropy()
visit_summary_tab

4.4. Retrieve schema from ExposureCatalog¶

As mentioned in section 2.1., the visit_summary schema can be retrieved directly from the ExposureCatalog object. This can be accessed directly as a lsst.afw.table.Schema object (uncomment below to inspect).

In [18]:
# visit_summary.schema

The schema can also be extracted from the astropy table. Access the schema information for each column and print out the details for the first column, id.

In [19]:
schema_tab = {}
for i_col, colname in enumerate(visit_summary_tab.colnames):
    schema_tab[i_col] = {}
    col = visit_summary_tab[colname]
    schema_tab[i_col]["name"] = colname
    schema_tab[i_col]["unit"] = col.unit
    schema_tab[i_col]["description"] = col.description
    schema_tab[i_col]["dtype"] = col.dtype
schema_tab[0]
Out[19]:
{'name': 'id',
 'unit': None,
 'description': 'unique ID',
 'dtype': dtype('int64')}
In [20]:
del visit_summary_tab, schema_tab

4.5. Get WCS from ExposureRecord¶

The ExposureCatalog consists of an ExposureRecord for each detector that was processed by the pipeline. Inspect the record for detector id=1.

In [21]:
detector_id = 1
record = visit_summary.find(detector_id)
record

In addition to the tabular data, the ExposureRecord has methods for extracting other information about that visit-detector, such as the WCS (see also tutorial 204.3.).

In [22]:
legacy_wcs = record.wcs
legacy_wcs
Out[22]:
FITS standard SkyWcs:
Sky Origin: (150.1966199433, +2.2490437847)
Pixel Origin: (nan, nan)
Pixel Scale: nan arcsec/pixel

Define the bounding box of the detector.

In [23]:
detector_bbox = Box.from_legacy(record.getBBox())
detector_bbox
Out[23]:
Box(y=Interval(start=0, stop=4000), x=Interval(start=0, stop=4072))

Combine the record WCS with a DetectorFrame object containing the visit-detector IDs and the detector bounding box to create an lsst.images SkyProjection object.

In [24]:
wcs_visit = SkyProjection.from_legacy(
    legacy_wcs,
    DetectorFrame(
        instrument="LSSTCam",
        visit=record.get("visit"),
        detector=record.get("id"),
        bbox=detector_bbox,
    ),
)
In [25]:
wcs_visit

The ExposureRecord can also be used to extract an astropy FITS compatible approximation of the visit-detector WCS.

In [27]:
fits_wcs_visit = wcs_visit.as_fits_wcs(detector_bbox, allow_approximation=True)
fits_wcs_visit

4.6. Get PSF from ExposureRecord¶

The PSF model for the visit-detector can also be extracted from the record (see also tutorial 205.2).

In [29]:
legacy_psf = record.getPsf()
legacy_psf
Out[29]:
<lsst.meas.extensions.piff.piffPsf.PiffPsf at 0x7ddceca83830>
In [30]:
psf = PointSpreadFunction.from_legacy(legacy_psf, bounds=detector_bbox)
psf
Out[30]:
PiffWrapper
├── bounds: [y=0:4000, x=0:4072]
└── kernel_bbox: [y=-13:14, x=-13:14]
In [31]:
del record, legacy_psf, psf, detector_bbox

5. Example use case: observation metadata across the focal plane¶

In addition to retrieving visit-detector WCS and PSF information, a possible use of visit_summary is to look at the variation in observation metadata across the focal plane of a given visit. For example, one can analyse how the average sky background, skyBg (adu), varies for each detector in a given visit.

As described in CTN-001 and tutorial 208.1. there are 189 science CCDs in the LSSTCam focal plane. However, the visit_summary ExposureCatalog will not contain 189 records, as only detectors that have been processed by the pipeline are recorded. Furthermore some detectors may be present in the ExposureCatalog but with NaN values for certain columns, depending on which parts of the pipeline were able to run successfully. Define an array of expected detector IDs for all 189 science detectors.

In [32]:
detector_ids = np.arange(189)
print(len(detector_ids))

189

Check which detectors are missing from ExposureCatalog for this visit.

In [33]:
missing_detectors = detector_ids[
    ~np.isin(detector_ids, np.array(visit_summary["id"]))
    ]
missing_detectors
Out[33]:
array([  0,  20,  27,  65, 120, 121, 122, 123, 161, 168, 188])

Detector id$=[0,20,27,65,123,161,168,188]$ corresponds to the 8 corners of the focal plane which are not processed due to vignetting. In addition to the corner detectors other detectors may have been excluded from processing; for visit=2025051500122 these are id$=[120,121,122]$. The number of missing detectors changes across DP2, but detector id=122 is consistently excluded due to a known overcurrent consistent with a short.

Additional information about each detector id, such as name and serial number, can be extracted from the Lsstcam object.

In [34]:
camera = LsstCam.getCamera()
cam_id_map = camera.getIdMap()

for det_id in missing_detectors:
    print(f"{det_id}: {cam_id_map[det_id].getName()}, "
          f"{cam_id_map[det_id].getSerial()}"
          )

0: R01_S00, ITL-3800C-083
20: R03_S02, ITL-3800C-467
27: R10_S00, ITL-3800C-466
65: R14_S02, E2V-CCD250-141
120: R30_S10, E2V-CCD250-358
121: R30_S11, E2V-CCD250-251
122: R30_S12, E2V-CCD250-149
123: R30_S20, E2V-CCD250-166
161: R34_S22, E2V-CCD250-311
168: R41_S20, ITL-3800C-443
188: R43_S22, ITL-3800C-076

To investigate the properties of this visit, make a plot that represents the extent of each detector in visit_summary across the focal plane and indicates the value of the chosen observation metadata parameter. The detectors are plotted as polygons, where RA and Dec positions are extracted from raCorners and decCorners. The id of each detector is indicated with text.

In [35]:
fig, ax = plt.subplots()

patches = []
for i_detector in range(len(visit_summary)):
    polygon = Polygon(
        np.array([visit_summary[i_detector]["raCorners"],
                  visit_summary[i_detector]["decCorners"]]).T
    )
    patches.append(polygon)

    x = visit_summary[i_detector]["ra"]
    y = visit_summary[i_detector]["dec"]
    t = visit_summary[i_detector]["id"]
    ax.text(
        x, y, t, fontsize=8,
        verticalalignment="center", horizontalalignment="center"
    )

colors = visit_summary["skyBg"]
p = PatchCollection(patches)
p.set_array(colors)
s1 = ax.add_collection(p)

cbar = plt.colorbar(s1)
cbar.set_label("skyBg (adu)")

ax.autoscale_view()
ax.set_xlabel("ra (degrees)")
ax.set_ylabel("dec (degrees)")

plt.title("visit={}".format(visit_summary.get("visit")[0]))

plt.show()

Figure 1: Plot of an LSSTCam visit with each detector in the visit displayed as a polygon as defined by the RA and Dec of its corners (this is a cartesian, not sky, projection). The detector-polygons are labeled by id and colored by an observational metadata parameter, in this case the average sky background, skyBg (adu), for each detector.

6. Exercises for the learner¶

  1. Repeat the analysis but for a visit with more missing detectors, e.g. visit=2025042400172.
  2. Recreate the Figure 1 for other observational metadata parameters, e.g. magLim, psfSigma or effTime. Take note of which metadata parameters may be NaN, depending on which parts of the pipeline successfully processed the detector.
In [ ]:
